topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture and outlines the intended learning outcomes regarding cancer treatment approaches.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and cytotoxic resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine conventional cancer treatment modalities, including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy, alongside the biological mechanisms responsible for systemic toxicity and drug efflux resistance.

topics.label: Exploiting cancer cell vulnerabilities and genetic defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain therapeutic strategies that exploit intrinsic vulnerabilities in cancer cells, including hormone receptor dependency, cell cycle checkpoint deficiencies, and defective DNA repair pathways.

topics.label: Oncogenic kinase targeting and resistance mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the design and application of small-molecule kinase inhibitors against oncogenic drivers and analyze the molecular mechanisms underlying therapy resistance and drug addiction.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine targeted antibody-based therapies, including naked monoclonal antibodies that trigger immune effector functions and antibody-drug conjugates that deliver cytotoxic payloads directly to tumor cells.

topics.label: Immune surveillance and checkpoint inhibition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the evidence for natural antitumor immune surveillance and describe how checkpoint inhibitors disinhibit endogenous T-cell responses against tumor neoantigens.

topics.label: Engineered T-cell therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail synthetic immunotherapeutic approaches, specifically bispecific T-cell engagers and chimeric antigen receptor T cells, designed to redirect cytotoxic immune responses against cancer cells.

topics.label: Clinical progress, systemic challenges, and future perspectives
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics synthesize the overarching achievements and limitations of modern oncology while outlining future paradigms in cancer management and clinical trial design.
